title: Conversation transfer & handshake — product sketch
body:
Context and problem
---
We have many points where a conversation started against Redwood's hosted API needs to move between different execution contexts: human agent to assistant, assistant-to-assistant (specialized skill), mobile->server handoff, and cross-region failovers. Today it's ad-hoc: teams either rehydrate from full history (expensive) or ship a proto-state that loses safety signals, identity, or cost controls.

Design goal
---
Make a lightweight, explicit "conversation transfer" primitive ("handshake") that:
- preserves minimal fidelity for continuity (short summary, pointers to important messages, anchors)
- includes operational metadata (source model id + version, token counts, applied transforms, cost bucket)
- supports human-in-the-loop annotations (agent notes, redactions)
- is cheap to serialize/transfer and can be rehydrated into any Redwood-compatible runtime (hosted, dedicated, or private)
- exposes guardrails for privacy/compliance (PII flags, KMS-wrapped blobs)

What this doc is
---
Rough PRD sketch + user stories + API/UX notes + rollout plan. Not final. Rapid open questions inlined. Notes-to-self included.

Personas
---
- Product engineer (mobile/web) who wants smooth continuity when users move devices or escalate to human support.
- Support agent who needs context bundled but filtered for privacy.
- Platform engineer who needs predictable perf and cost accounting when sessions jump between tenancy types.

Success metrics (initial)
---
- >90% of escalations from bot->human have <3s perceived context load time for agents (measured via agent UI telemetry).
- 50% reduction in tokens sent during handoff vs naive full-history rehydrate for target flows.
- No PII leakage incidents in first 6 months for customers opt-in to handshake (internal audit).

User stories
---
1) Mobile app: "When I open a support chat on my phone that I started on desktop, the assistant remembers the last 3 messages and the selected persona."
   - Acceptance: agent sees session summary + 3 recent messages, token counts, and a link to full history if requested (permissioned).
2) Support agent workflow: "Agent receives concise redacted summary and my last action items, can click 'Load full' which requests additional data with approval flow."
   - Acceptance: default view redacted; 'load full' initiates audit-loggable call; agent must confirm receipt.
3) Skill chaining: "When engine A finishes, it transfers a compact 'result' package to engine B that only contains necessary state (slots filled, blocking errors)."
   - Acceptance: downstream model continues with correct slot values without needing earlier transcript.
4) Cross-region failover: "If region X becomes unhealthy, sessions can move to region Y with persisted minimal state and fallback model id mapping."
   - Acceptance: observable in rollout dashboards; <1% error during planned failover tests.

Handshake payload sketch (minimal)
---
- handshake_id: uuid (opaque)
- source_model: model-name@sha or alias
- token_stats: {estimated_prompt_tokens, kv_cache_bytes}  <-- store as flat fields in implementation
- anchors: list of short anchors/labels (3-5 strings)
- summary: 1-paragraph automated summary (string)
- redaction_map: list of indices/labels marked PII (list of simple strings)
- attachments: optional encrypted blob reference (kms_key_id + s3-like uri)
- provenance: originating_route, request_id, timestamp, owner_customer_id
- ops_flags: cost_bucket, priority, allow_full_rehydrate(bool)

Implementation notes (runtime)
---
- Handshake should be stored as compact JSON plus optional encrypted blob. Keep under 16KB uncompressed as a goal.
- When transferring between hosted -> dedicated, augment handshake with compatibility hints (e.g., quantized model variant).
- On rehydrate, runtime should optionally fetch attachments lazily.

API sketch (developer ergonomics)
---
- POST /v1/sessions/{session_id}/handshake -> creates handshake; returns handshake_id + signed-url if large blob attached
- GET /v1/handshakes/{handshake_id} -> metadata and summary
- POST /v1/handshakes/{handshake_id}/accept -> target runtime consumes handshake and returns resume_token for continued requests
- headers: X-Redwood-Trace, X-Customer-KMS-Policy
- RBAC: only principals in allowlist can call accept; default is restrictive

UX & Agent UI notes
---
- Default agent panel shows: conversation headline (auto-generated), confidence score, redacted snippet, 'Load more' button with audit popup.
- Allow agents to add an "agent note" that becomes an immutable part of the handshake provenance.
- For mobile -> mobile, provide a 'fast transfer' that only moves anchors + last 2 messages; for human escalation provide richer package.

Privacy / compliance
---
- Default behavior: PII flagged at source by text detector, stripped from handshake summary but included in encrypted attachments.
- Option: customer toggles 'allow-full-rehydrate' per workspace.
- Audit logs for every accept/retrieve of encrypted attachments (satisfy enterprise audit).

Rollout plan (MVP -> v1)
---
MVP (4 sprints)
- Minimal handshake schema + server endpoints for create/get/accept
- Agent UI mock + manual rehydrate flow (SRE only)
- PII tagging plugin (existing detector) to mark redactions
- Metrics: payload size, tokens saved, agent load time

v1 (next 6-8 weeks)
- Support encrypted attachments + KMS integration
- RBAC + per-customer allowlist controls in Console
- Deduped fallback mapping for model variants
- SDK helper functions (python/js) to create/accept handshakes

Anti-requirements (what this is NOT)
---
- Not a full conversation database migration tool. It should not attempt to replicate entire conversation transcripts by default.
- Not a replacement for customer-managed audit & retention policies — should integrate with them.

Risks & mitigations
---
- Risk: Handshake becomes a vector for exfiltrating sensitive tokens.
  Mitigation: Enforce KMS-wrapping for attachments, limit handshake lifetime, require allowlist.
- Risk: Increased ops complexity across Dedicated/Private.
  Mitigation: Provide best-effort compatibility hints and fallbacks; surface warnings in Console when acceptance is cross-deployment.

Open questions (quick list)
---
- Who is the canonical owner of handshake storage? (hosted control plane vs customer-managed blobstore)
- TTL defaults — 24h? 7d? depend on use-case.
- How to represent partial rehydrates in billing & telemetry? (estimate vs exact tokens)
- Should we allow signed short-lived tokens for third-party tools to request attachments?

Next steps / TODOs
---
- [ ] Sync with SRE on storage SLA and cross-region replication (ASSIGN: Oliver)
- [ ] Proto API + Postman collection (ASSIGN: Noor)
- [ ] UX quick prototype for agent panel (ASSIGN: Maya)
- [ ] Small perf experiment: measure token size reduction for 10 common flows (ASSIGN: Ravi)
- [ ] Draft Console controls page mockup and permit list UX copy (ASSIGN: product-design)
notes_to_self: keep this light — focus on MVP that solves agent continuity without shipping entire transcript
